entity: Ithaca (ithaca.deepmind.com, now served at predictingthepast.com), the deep neural network of DeepMind and academic partners (Ca' Foscari University of Venice, the University of Oxford, the Athens University of Economics and Business) for the textual restoration, geographical attribution and chronological attribution of ancient Greek inscriptions, presented in Nature on 9 March 2022 (Assael, Sommerschield et al., 'Restoring and attributing ancient texts using deep neural networks', Nature 603, 280–283), trained on I.PHI (78,608 inscriptions from the Packard Humanities Institute's dataset), its code open under Apache 2.0; formalized in the Revelation First meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-30 (https://www.revelationfirst.com/aggregators/ithaca/). Distinct from Ithaca the island and Homer's Ithaca, after which it is named, from Ithaca, New York, and from the other homonyms of the bare name; the operator's address adds the disambiguator 'DeepMind'

classes_note: Three classes, each the census's own intersection, evidence kind, text object, method or stated limit for the entity, stated by field sources at the loci given: (1) AI models for ancient texts (census intersection 'ai-ancient-texts', evidence_kind 'machine reading, restoration or dating', worked question 'machine-dating'; B4, B1, B3, B5); (2) Greek inscriptions (census text_object, negative_tags; B4, B1, B3); (3) machine assistance to historians (census stated_limits, method; B4, B1, B3). The archive bears on these classes through the Revelation First thesis (#202 and the deposits revelationfirst.com cites: the dating and priority of the New Testament writings), its Sappho and papyrological work, and its machine-reading work; a deposit enters only where its sentence says something of the entity or applies its category to one of these classes. The census's rf_intersection ('Machine dating of Greek text: inscriptions, not manuscripts. A method the dating workstream can watch ...') and correction are the archive's reading, ledgered as RF-; they do not by themselves admit a deposit. Aliases: the name, case-sensitive (every hit is read; uses of the island, Homer's Ithaca, Cavafy's poem or the city are the homonyms' and rejected), the model's dataset (I.PHI), the paper's title, the DeepMind post's title and the paper's co-first authors. Aeneas, DeepMind's later Latin model, is a neighbour entity (census relation), not an alias; its string enters only class (1). Admission by reading (§3.4): a bare mention, a reference-list entry or a keyword is not a claim.
